english.title: Owner / master / operator broadcast from British registered ship not in / over UK / external waters
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) you

(A)_[were the owner of a British-registered ship from]_
(B)_[were the master of a British-registered ship from]_
(C)_[operated the apparatus on a British-registered ship by means of]_
(D)_[participated in the operation of the apparatus on a British-registered ship by means of]_

which a broadcast has been made while it was not

(E)_[in]_
(F)_[over]_

(G)_[the United Kingdom]_
(H)_[external waters]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 77(1)(b) and (2) and 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that proceedings in England and Wales for this offence may be brought only by OFCOM or by or with the consent of the Secretary of State or the DPP.
(ii) Section 77(5) of the Act provides that master, in relation to a ship, includes any other person (except the pilot) who has command or charge of the ship; and operator, in relation to an aircraft, means the person who at the relevant time has the management of the aircraft.
(iii) Section 115(8) of the Act provides that apparatus on board a ship includes apparatus on a kite or captive balloon flown from the ship.
(iv) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(v) Section 94 of the Act provides a saving for broadcasts made under and in accordance with a wireless telegraphy licence.
(vi) The Wireless Telegraphy (Fixed Penalty) Regulations 2011, (In force 01/10/2011), introduces a £100-00p fixed penalty charge for summary only offences under the Act, as from that date. This regime does not include offences relating to illegal broadcasting (pirate radio).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

Fixed Penalty charge of £100-00p (in force from 01/10/2011).

For offences committed before the commencement of section 282(3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003:
Six months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
